title: Adaptive trace normalizer for format translation and sampling metrics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Redwood receives trace data from many sources: legacy Jaeger thrift/proto collectors, applications that emit OTLP but with older semantic conventions, and third-party vendors with custom tags. Our existing ingestion paths expect OTLP and sometimes drop or mis-map fields (e.g. legacy 'service_name' tags, nonstandard span attributes). This leads to sampling mismatch, broken trace linking across services, and inconsistent dashboards.

Goal: Build an "adaptive trace normalizer" service that sits in front of collectors and: 1) detects incoming trace format (Jaeger thrift/proto, OTLP/gRPC, HTTP JSON), 2) translates/normalizes spans to a consistent OTLP v1.0 representation while preserving important legacy tags, 3) deterministically maps trace/span IDs when necessary to maintain cross-system linkage, 4) preserves sampling metadata and surface it to downstream collectors, and 5) emits operational metrics (conversion_rate, conversion_errors, dropped_spans_by_reason, format_detect_latency) for alerting and dashboards.

Non-goals: Replacing full OTLP relay functionality (rate-limits/backpressure are limited to defensive buffering and backoff; long-term routing policies remain a separate project).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Normalizer accepts Jaeger thrift/proto, OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP JSON and produces OTLP v1.0 proto on the output path.
2) Deterministic trace ID mapping implemented for 64->128-bit backward compatibility with config toggle; cross-service traces remain joinable in test harness.
3) Sampling metadata is preserved as attributes and exposes a new sample.probability metric and an attribute sample.source.
4) Metrics emitted to Prometheus: normalizer_conversion_total, normalizer_conversion_errors_total, normalizer_dropped_spans_total, normalizer_format_detect_latency_seconds (histogram).
5) Integration tests exercise 3 real collector targets (tempo, legacy jaeger-collector, and third-party SaaS) with synthetic traffic and assert no more than 0.2% attribute loss and 99th percentile translation latency < 15ms under steady load.
6) Canary deployment manifests and runbook documented in /confluence/observability/normalizer-canary.
7) Design review approved and security review completed (PII/PII-redaction checklist).
implementation_steps:
1) API + detector: add lightweight format detector with pluggable parsers (Go, internal pkg).
2) Translator library: implement tag->attribute mapping table and deterministic id mapper in go/tracing/normalizer.
3) Metrics: add Prometheus instrumentation and wire to console dashboards.
4) Resilience: implement small bounded buffer, backoff to downstream collectors, and config-driven drop policies.
5) Tests: unit tests for mapping, fuzz tests for malformed frames, and multi-target integration test harness.
6) Docs & runbook: canary steps, rollback criteria, alert thresholds.
7) Rollout: canary to a single region and customer cohort, monitor for schema regressions for 72h.
notes:
- Implementation language: Go (aligns with existing trace relay services).
- We will reuse parts of the existing span-enrichment shim (ENG-13658) for tag normalization.
- Deterministic ID mapping: default disabled. When enabled it will map 64-bit trace IDs to 128-bit by left-padding with a configured prefix; rationale documented in design doc.
- We must ensure we do not accidentally surface sensitive fields; redaction pipeline from security will run as a post-normalize step.
- Performance target: steady-state CPU < 1 vCPU per 10k spans/s for the normalizer container.
